sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A large evergreen tree, about 40–60 m tall, with a tiered crown and leathery leaves in whorls of roughly four to eight. Fragrant white-to-cream flowers cluster at branch tips. Paired follicles, about 20–63 cm long, split to release silky-haired seeds. It is native from tropical and subtropical Asia to northern Australia and the Solomon Islands.

sections.title: Uses and safety
sections.text: The wood is used for household items and paper. Injured parts exude irritating white latex, and the strongly scented flowers can cause sensitivity in some people. No food use is established in the sources consulted.
